newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-FANIE GOES UP THE POLE FOR CHARITY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-FANIE GOES UP THE POLE FOR CHARITY.

text.p: South African cricketer Fanie de Villiers has gone up the pole to raise funds for a child deafness charity.

The 32-year-old fast bowler, currently out of the test team but hoping for a recall to the one-day side, is spending the final three days of the third test against Australia at Centurion Park camped on top of one of the ground's 50-metre floodlight pylons.

"I'm not coming down until the selectors put me back in the team," joked De Villiers who has already raised hundreds of thousands of rands for the charity with a sponsored cycle ride around South Africa
His young daughter Sune was given back her hearing after a successful implant.
De Villiers' "pole-sitting" was reported on CNN television, resulting in one pledge of 100,000 rands (22,600 dollars) from overseas.
